scope_summary: Accessibility, first use and visitor-facing content of the audited build (f10fe585..., 43e3e5b), by real input on visitor pages at 1600x900, 1280x720, browser zoom 200% (800x450 at density 2), 400% (400x225 at 4), WCAG's reflow width (320x256 at 4) and an emulated phone (390x844, 844x390); the whole Tab cycle with Chromium's computed names; hover-only information; target sizes; small and clipped text; touch gestures near the timeline; forced colours and reduced motion; the words a visitor reads, confirmed as drawn. Headless Chromium 141 on SwiftShader, on a heavily shared 4-core container: no time is a device's; the phone is desktop emulation, not a mobile browser; no screen reader or other assistive technology was available. Earlier automated coverage (check:contrast 45 states, the self-test's A-1..A-6/SW checks) was not repeated.

findings.title: At 400% browser zoom and at WCAG's 320 px reflow width the interface loses content and functions (the card's start, the phase text, the caption, the key, the panels, the sources)
findings.subsystem: layout (style.css short-viewport rules, app.js syncDock), first-run card, timeline control row, tools
findings.user_impact: A low-vision visitor who zooms a desktop browser to 400% cannot read the first card's heading and opening lines, never sees the phase's narrative, the caption or the key, and cannot open the panels (order of battle, analysis, command, plans) or 'Accuracy and sources' with the pointer: most of the map's explanation is gone.
refs: style.css:619-625 (max-height:430px: .dispatch and .legend display:none)
style.css:645-648 (#firstrun anchored to the timeline's top, no max-height or overflow below 431 px tall)
style.css:851-862 (held-landscape block: the query is the height's alone, so a zoomed desktop window takes it; #eyesbtn hidden)
app.js:8971-8984 (syncDock: below 1080 px the Now tab is hidden and the dispatch is the card)
shell.html:116-134 (the tools column, which wraps under the timeline)
findings.evidence: docs/audit-post8-evidence/a11y/zoom.json (steps 400x225-at4:* and 320x256-at4:*); docs/audit-post8-evidence/a11y/zoom-400x225-at4-1-first.jpg, zoom-400x225-at4-2-explore.jpg, zoom-320x256-at4-2-explore.jpg; 200% for comparison: zoom-800x450-at2-*.jpg
findings.repro: Visitor page (no ?harness=1), Chromium context viewport 400x225 at deviceScaleFactor 4 (a 1600x900 screen at 400%) and 320x256 at 4 (1280x1024 at 400%); wait for the card; screenshot; press Esc (real key); then a real click on the Panels button's centre and on 'Accuracy and sources'.
findings.expected: WCAG 1.4.10 (AA): at 320 CSS px wide nothing but the two-dimensional map itself may need two-dimensional scrolling or be lost: the card scrolls inside itself, the phase text stays reachable (the phone layout's grip sheet does this at 390 px), every control stays on screen and pressable.
findings.observed: 400x225 (400%): the card's box starts at y=-112 (height 228, not scrollable; the page has overflow hidden), so its heading and first lines are off screen; after Esc no phase text, situation or events anywhere (.dispatch display:none, no Now tab); caption 0 px wide; no key; the Panels button under the timeline (hit-test div.tb-top at 3 of 3 points; a real click opened nothing); '?' partly off screen; the timeline 40% of the height. 320x256: the card starts at y=-140; '?' off screen (x=370); Panels opens a rail whose scrolling area is 0 px tall and 'Accuracy and sources' sits under the timeline (a real click opened nothing). The phone held landscape (844x390) also shows no phase text. 200% (800x450) passes: everything reachable (1.4.4 met).
findings.remedy: By size, not by device: give #firstrun a max-height with overflow:auto at heights of 430 px or less; keep the phase text reachable there (the phone's grip sheet, or the Now tab in the rail); below 720 px wide put the tools, '?' and 'Whose eyes?' behind the Menu whatever the height, or let the timeline's control row wrap; keep the rail's scrolling area a usable height (or take the brand and tabs out of it at small heights). Add a 320x256 and a 400x225 case to check:visual.
findings.effort: 1-3 days (layout, then the visual harness's limits re-measured)
findings.risk: medium: the phone and held-landscape layouts share these rules (decisions 223-226, 232); their cases must hold
findings.validation: zoom.js again: card fully on screen or scrollable, narr.lede reachable in one press, every control on screen and pressable at 400x225 and 320x256; check:visual's phone cases unchanged
findings.cause_hypothesis: The short-viewport rules (Stage 0, kept by decision 226 for a phone held landscape) hide the dispatch and the key on any window 430 px tall or less, and Stage 3C moved the situation strip into the dispatch, so the Stage 0 comment's premise ('the situation strip keeps the narrative') no longer holds; the phone layout that solves this is gated on min-height 431 px.
findings.cause_verified: partly: the rules and the gate read in style.css and app.js; the outcome measured

findings.title: Caveats a reader needs are given only in hover tooltips (title attributes): the derived readings' warnings, the vantages' 'not what he saw', the cut caption's full text, why relief is disabled
findings.subsystem: interface text (app.js paintSituation, shell.html tools, fitCaption)
findings.user_impact: Keyboard and touch visitors never see that the 'derived' figures are spatial readings, not casualty figures, nor that the Zuran and Allied vantages are not what the commanders saw; screen-reader users get them as descriptions, mouse users only by resting the pointer.
refs: app.js:7347-7348 (SEP_NOTE, FLAT_NOTE)
app.js:7368-7370 (written only into title= on span.der, not focusable)
app.js:7380 (the same spans in the Now tab's situation line)
shell.html:129-131 (van-btn titles: 'a preset view, not what he saw', 'not what the Allied staff saw')
app.js:2581 (relief buttons disabled with the reason in title)
app.js:5639 (the squeezed key's reason in title)
app.js:5724 (an evidence-skeleton anchor's clock and grade as the canvas's title)
app.js:7378 (cap.title=capTitle(cap): the full caption)
findings.evidence: docs/audit-post8-evidence/a11y/fu-1600x900.json step 1 'titles' (25 elements whose title adds words not in their name or visible text); docs/audit-post8-evidence/a11y/zoom-1280x720-at1-caption-crop.jpg (caption cut to 'THE DECEPT… · D. ·')
findings.expected: Information that qualifies a figure or a view is visible text, or reachable by focus and by touch (a toggletip button, or the sentence in the Now tab and the eye-level caption); native title tooltips are a supplement only.
findings.observed: span.der carries FLAT_NOTE ('The reconstruction plots formations, not losses. A holding that does not change does not mean the fighting there has stopped.') and SEP_NOTE ('...A spatial reading, not a casualty figure.') in title only; the spans take no focus; on a phone no tooltip exists. The vantage buttons' integrity caveats are titles (Chromium exposes them as accessible descriptions). At 1280x720 the caption reads 'THE DECEPT… · D. · interval Friant's division at Raigern since the ni…'; its full text is the title.
findings.remedy: Show FLAT_NOTE/SEP_NOTE as visible text in the Now tab (or a focusable 'what is this?' toggletip); put the vantages' caveat into the camera's own caption when a preset is chosen; give disabled relief buttons a visible hint or keep them enabled with a message.
findings.validation: keyboard-only and touch walk-through finds each caveat without a pointer

As drawn in the full dossiers' 'Dated by' rows at a clock inside each move: '(moveMin)' (Imperial Headquarters, 12:10), 'Until roadmap step 4b ... (question 177)' and '... was the phase-2 entry ...' (Friant, 07:00 and 09:20), 'Until roadmap step 4b's question 202 ... findings.title: On a phone the event markers' hit areas cover most of the time rail, so a finger dragged along the rail does not scrub the clock and a tap on it jumps to an event instead
findings.subsystem: timeline (style.css .ev-mark hit area, app.js time rail pointer handlers)
findings.user_impact: The phone's time rail cannot be dragged over most of the day; visitors fall back on Play, the event steps and the phase list.
refs: style.css:379-382 (.evmarks over the rail; .ev-mark 8 px rotated, its ::after inset -6px, pointer-events auto)
style.css:794 (phone: rail and markers at the same top)
app.js:7528-7530 (the rail scrubs only from its own pointerdown)
findings.evidence: docs/audit-post8-evidence/a11y/phone2.json steps 2-3; docs/audit-post8-evidence/a11y/phone.json step 'horizontal drag 200 px on the time rail' (before the zoom); coverage computed from the 21 distinct event starts and the markers' hit geometry (README, Phone)
findings.repro: Phone page (390x844, density 3, touch); close the card; CDP touch drag along the rail from 22% to 72% of its width at its vertical centre; then a page.touchscreen tap at 30%.
findings.expected: A drag anywhere on the rail scrubs (markers yield to a moving finger, or take presses only on a tap), as on desktop between markers.
findings.observed: Two real touch drags along the rail (phone.js, phone2.js) left the clock unchanged; a tap at 30% hit button.ev-mark.dec and set 08:25. At the rail's centre line the markers' hit areas (16 px wide there) cover 66% of the 374 px phone rail and 91% of it between 07:00 and 15:00 (24% and 34% of the 1,572 px desktop rail).
findings.remedy: Let a drag that starts on a marker scrub (handle pointerdown on .evmarks, decide tap or drag by movement), or raise the markers above the rail band on touch layouts.
findings.risk: low-medium (the markers' keyboard group and 2.5.8 essential exception unchanged)
findings.validation: phone touch drag scrubs from any point; a tap on a marker still opens its event

findings.title: Two-finger gestures on the phone: in Chromium's touch emulation a pinch zoomed the whole page (visual viewport x3.3 to x5) and never the map; no check has ever driven the map's pinch with browser-level touch input
findings.subsystem: touch input (app.js bindCanvas pinch, style.css touch-action)
findings.user_impact: If a real phone behaves as the emulation did, a visitor who pinches to zoom the map zooms the interface instead and must pinch back; the map's own zoom by pinch would be unreachable.
refs: style.css:8 (canvas touch-action:none)
style.css:344 (the rail touch-action:none; the rest of the timeline default)
app.js:6854-6890 (bindCanvas: the pinch from two tracked touch pointers)
app.js:9258-9266 (the self-test's pinch: synthetic PointerEvents dispatched in the page, not browser input)
findings.evidence: docs/audit-post8-evidence/a11y/phone2.json steps 1 and 4-5 (one-finger drag on the map panned the camera: CDP touches reach the app; a pinch on the map alone: camera unchanged, visualViewport.scale 1 -> 3.259; a pinch with one finger starting on the timeline: 3.259 -> 3.918); docs/audit-post8-evidence/a11y/phone.json step 'pinch out: one finger on the timeline' (1 -> 5, the following taps then missed); docs/audit-post8-evidence/a11y/phone2-05-after-timeline-pinch.jpg
findings.repro: Phone context (390x844, density 3, isMobile, hasTouch, iPhone user agent), visitor page, card closed; CDP Input.dispatchTouchEvent touchStart with two points (160,360) and (230,430), ten touchMove steps spreading them 50 px, touchEnd; read landCam.position and visualViewport.scale.
findings.expected: A pinch on the map zooms the map (touch-action:none on the canvas keeps the browser out); a pinch beginning on the interface may zoom the page (that is the visitor's zoom, which should stay available).
findings.observed: Map-only pinch: camera position unchanged, page zoomed x3.26. One finger on the timeline: page zoomed further. The emulation's handling of multi-touch touch-action is itself uncertain, so this is not a device result.
findings.remedy: Test pinch-to-zoom on a real iPhone and Android phone (the owner's devices); if confirmed, check that the canvas receives both pointers (no element between), and that the page's own zoom stays possible from the panels.
findings.risk: unknown until reproduced on a device

findings.title: Forced colours (high contrast): the app has no forced-colors handling; the Layers panel's on/off rows and ground buttons, the speed, Follow and the current phase lose their state, 22 of 25 event markers vanish, and the key's swatches and the side marks before names become identical white squares
findings.subsystem: style.css (no @media (forced-colors) rule; colour carried by backgrounds)
findings.user_impact: A Windows High Contrast user cannot tell which layers are on, which ground is drawn, which speed is set or whether Follow is on, loses the timeline's event markers, and loses the French/Allied cue on labels and in the key (the map canvas keeps its own colours).
refs: style.css:380-388 (.ev-mark drawn by background:var(--side-fr|al))
shell.html:369 (the card's swatches)
style.css (no forced-colors rule; no forced-color-adjust anywhere: fc.json fcaNone 0)
findings.evidence: docs/audit-post8-evidence/a11y/fc.json (forced: true; no element with forced-color-adjust:none; swatches rgb(255,255,255) with black borders; pressed backgrounds opaque against translucent ones); docs/audit-post8-evidence/a11y/fc-01-first.jpg (key and side marks as white squares), fc-05-timebar.jpg (3 of 25 event diamonds; ½× and Follow like their neighbours), fc-09-layers.jpg (on and off rows alike), fc-08-legend.jpg, fc-03-viewmode.jpg, fc-04-tools.jpg
findings.expected: Under forced-colors: active, markers and swatches keep a visible, distinct form (system colours for borders, forced-color-adjust:none for the nation swatches and side marks, or text glyphs).
findings.observed: Chromium's emulation, light palette, no forced-color-adjust anywhere: the key's and the card's nation swatches and the side squares before formation names are all rgb(255,255,255); 22 of 25 event markers vanish (only the bordered decision diamonds remain); on the timeline the pressed ½×, Follow and the current phase look like their neighbours; in the Layers panel on and off rows look alike and Landscape like Paper map. Over the map a pressed button stays distinguishable (opaque against translucent neighbours over the dark canvas); tabs keep a weight difference; the focus ring stays (2 px, forced highlight).
findings.remedy: An @media (forced-colors: active) block: pressed and selected states by a system-colour border or outline (Highlight) or a glyph, not by background alone (the layer rows, the mode, speed and vantage buttons, Follow, the current phase); borders on .ev-mark; forced-color-adjust:none on the nation swatches and side marks (their colours are content).
findings.validation: fc.js again; on Windows with a contrast theme

findings.title: Panels opened from the keyboard do not take the focus or announce themselves: Layers (role=dialog) is reached only on the sixth Tab after its button, and a dossier opened by Enter on a map item leaves focus on the item, about 30 Tabs from the dossier (or Shift+Tab back past the earlier map items and the map group)
findings.subsystem: tools and the Layers panel (app.js setPop, shell.html order)
findings.user_impact: A keyboard or screen-reader user who opens Layers, or selects a formation on the map with Enter, is not taken to what opened and hears nothing about it; the dossier sits before the map layer in the DOM, so Tab goes on through the map items and round the whole page first.
refs: app.js:7070-7075 (setPop: hidden and aria-expanded set, no focus move)
shell.html:116-134 (#tools with the vantage group) and shell.html:137 (#layerpop after them in the DOM)
findings.evidence: docs/audit-post8-evidence/a11y/mapfocus.json step 'Layers by keyboard' (open: hidden false, expanded true, focus on #layersbtn; Tab x7: Field, Zuran, Pratzen, Allied, Overview, then the panel's x and Landscape) and step 'a formation's map item ... Enter' (selection f:gqg, drawer on, focus still on the map item); docs/audit-post8-evidence/a11y/kbd-h-1600x900.json step 'Layers: open, Tab, Esc'; DOM order shell.html:325 (aside.drawer) before shell.html:384 (main, the map layer)
findings.repro: Harness page 1600x900, card closed by Esc; focus #layersbtn (set-up), press Enter, then Tab seven times (real keys).
findings.expected: The opened panel next in the focus order (focus moved to its first control, or the panel placed right after its button), as a disclosure or non-modal dialog does (WCAG 2.4.3).
findings.remedy: On opening by keyboard, focus the panel's first control (Layers) and the dossier's heading (a map item's Enter), giving focus back on close as setPop and the dossier already do from inside; or move #layerpop to follow #layersbtn in the DOM.
findings.risk: low (the self-test's SW-5 focus rules must still hold)

findings.title: First use: neither the card nor the opening says the map is a reconstruction or what the A/B/C letters beside names mean; the key starts closed
findings.user_impact: A first-time visitor sees grade letters (B, C) on the names and 'derived' tags from the first screen with no explanation until they open the key, the sources sheet or reach the guided tour's ninth stop.
refs: shell.html:366-374 (the card and its words)
app.js:4710 (OPENING.stops [0,5,6,7])

app.js:5016 (ML.legendOpen false: the key opens closed, decision 49)
findings.expected: One sentence on the primary path (card or opening's first step): positions are reconstructed and graded A/B/C (the letters by the names), and where the sources are.
findings.observed: Card: colour key and the Pratzen plateau 'which this map reads as deciding the battle'. Opening steps 1-4: battlefield, the French strike, the army divided, the collapse; none mentions reconstruction or grades. The key is collapsed ('Key +'); the grades are explained in it, in the sources sheet's second paragraph and in tour stop 9, which the opening does not include.

findings.user_impact: A visitor who turned the shortcuts off (as WCAG 2.1.4 lets them) is told to press a key that is now inert; a mouse or touch user is told to press a key at all.

findings.expected: A hint that is true in every state: a 'Show the phase text' button (or 'Esc shows everything'), its words from LABELS according to SHORTCUTS.on, naming the opening when the opening runs.

findings.title: Accessible names and structure: the tablist is named 'The rail', the key's toggle is read 'Key plus/minus', Play becomes 'Pause' while also pressed, the full dossier's headings carry their tag word ('How many record', 'Where reconstruction'), the narrative sits inside the navigation landmark and the tools outside any landmark, and below 1080 px the page has no h1
findings.user_impact: Screen-reader users hear internal jargon ('The rail, tab list'), a stray 'plus', 'Pause, toggle button, pressed', and find the phase text under 'Army and map controls' navigation rather than the main landmark (which holds only the map layer).
refs: shell.html:48 (aria-label="The rail")
style.css:689-690 (.lg-head::after '−'/'+' joins the name)
app.js:8793 (textContent 'Pause' with aria-pressed true)
shell.html:38-104 (nav.rail holds the h1, the tabs and the Now tab's narrative)
shell.html:384 (main holds only #maplayer)
app.js:7065, 8979 (rail-hidden below 1080 px: the rail, with the h1, leaves the tree)
findings.evidence: docs/audit-post8-evidence/a11y/kbd-h-1600x900-axtree.json and kbd-1600x900-axtree.json (Chromium's tree: 'tablist The rail', 'button Key +', landmarks navigation/region/main); docs/audit-post8-evidence/a11y/fu-1600x900.json step 'Play (real click)' (name 'Pause', aria-pressed true); docs/audit-post8-evidence/a11y/fc.json full-dossier step (headings 'H3 Who record', 'H3 How many record', 'H3 Where reconstruction', 'H3 Its day derived')
findings.expected: Plain names ('Panels' or 'Map panels'); the key's state by aria-expanded alone; Play/Pause either a changing label or a pressed state, not both; the narrative in main or a named region; one h1 at every width.
findings.observed: As in the title. Not a WCAG A/AA failure on its own (names exist; states are exposed); no screen reader was run.

not_checked: No screen reader or other assistive technology (NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver, TalkBack, speech input, switch access) was available: names, roles and live regions were read from Chromium's tree, not heard; docs/step3-evidence/sr-session.md holds no item results.
No real mobile browser: the phone is desktop Chromium emulating an iPhone; Safari/WebKit's touch-action, pinch and VoiceOver behaviour unverified (A11Y-05).
Forced colours only in Chromium's emulation (its default light palette), not Windows contrast themes or Firefox.
Firefox and Safari not run; no GPU; every time here is SwiftShader on a container shared by other jobs (load average 18-37).
Text-only zoom (1.4.4 by text size alone) not emulated; page zoom stands in for it.
The opening's played stretches were cut short by 'Next again' (each would take many real minutes here); the self-test holds them.
Live-region announcements were read as DOM text, not heard; their timing and duplication by a screen reader unverified.
Cognitive load, plain-language reading level and colour-vision simulations were not measured beyond the words read here.
strengths: Every control stop named; no keyboard trap; the two sheets and the card are real modal dialogs that contain focus and give it back; closing a dossier by Esc, x or Back hands focus to a shown control, never to the body.
The single-key shortcuts switch works as WCAG 2.1.4 asks (verified by real keys: '2' did nothing with it off).
Desktop targets all 24 px or spaced but the decided exceptions; the phone layout's targets 44 px; no horizontal scroll at any size; 200% zoom fully usable.

Claim words are plain and honest ('Read in a source', 'This map's reading', 'Not yet checked'); every dossier has 'How this is sourced' at its head; the sources sheet explains the grades in its second paragraph.
The map layer's 18 keyboard stops are drawn on screen and topmost once a frame is drawn (A-2 fixed); the timeline's tips appear on focus as well as hover.
